architecture_summary.operational_context: Multi-cloud (AWS Kinesis, GCP Pub/Sub) hybrid data platform with streaming/batch processing, ML model serving, and BI analytics. Deployed across AWS and GCP with shared Kafka backbone.

threat_actors.name: External Cybercriminal Group
threat_actors.motivation: Financial gain through data theft, ransomware, or cryptomining
threat_actors.initial_access_vector: Exploit public-facing ingestion endpoints (API webhook, SFTP gateway) or compromised credentials for Kinesis/PubSub producers
non_capabilities: No physical access to cloud infrastructure
No pre-existing valid credentials for IAM service
Cannot directly access VPC-private storage tiers

threat_actors.name: Malicious Insider (Data Engineer)
threat_actors.motivation: Intellectual property theft, sabotage, or data exfiltration for personal gain
threat_actors.initial_access_vector: Legitimate access to Airflow orchestrator, Kafka Connect, or Spark/Flink job submission
non_capabilities: Cannot bypass IAM service policy enforcement without privilege escalation
No access to cloud provider root accounts
Cannot modify ML model registry without audit trail
No ability to disable platform-wide encryption at rest

threat_actors.name: Adversarial ML Attacker
threat_actors.motivation: Model evasion, data poisoning, or model extraction to compromise ML-driven decisions
threat_actors.initial_access_vector: API calls to ML serving endpoint, poisoned training data via feature store, or supply chain compromise of model registry
non_capabilities: No direct access to Flink/Spark processing clusters
Cannot modify Airflow DAGs or Kafka topics directly
No ability to extract model weights without API access
Cannot bypass model registry signature verification

attack_paths.entry_point: Unauthenticated API webhook endpoint exposed to internet
attack_paths.impact: Remote code execution on webhook receiver, pivot to Kafka cluster
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Webhook receiver is internet-facing with potential deserialization vulnerabilities; no WAF depicted

attack_paths.entry_point: Stolen producer credentials for Kinesis/PubSub connectors
attack_paths.impact: Unauthorized data injection into Kafka topics, downstream poisoning
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Credentials managed by external producers; rotation and monitoring not shown

attack_paths.entry_point: Compromised SFTP gateway via weak credentials or CVE
attack_paths.impact: Persistent foothold in ingestion tier, file upload manipulation
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: SFTP gateways often have weak auth; direct path to Kafka Connect

attack_paths.entry_point: Malicious Flink job submitted via compromised Airflow or direct API
attack_paths.impact: Arbitrary code execution in processing tier, access to raw data lake
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Airflow orchestrates Flink; insider or compromised Airflow can submit jobs

attack_paths.entry_point: Compromised Flink/Spark job or direct storage API access
attack_paths.impact: Exfiltration of raw confidential data from data lake
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Raw zone contains unprocessed sensitive data; broad read access for processing

attack_paths.entry_point: Compromised BI dashboard service account or SQL injection in dashboard queries
attack_paths.impact: Exfiltration of curated business data, PII, financial records
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: BI dashboard has read access to warehouse; service accounts often over-privileged

attack_paths.entry_point: Poisoned data injected via Kafka -> Flink -> feature store pipeline
attack_paths.impact: Model degradation, biased predictions, targeted misclassification
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Feature store feeds ML models; data quality checker may not detect targeted poisoning

attack_paths.entry_point: Compromised CI/CD pipeline or insider upload of backdoored model artifact
attack_paths.impact: Persistent backdoor in production models, triggered by specific inputs
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Requires supply chain compromise or malicious insider with registry write access

attack_paths.entry_point: Malicious producer injecting corrupted Avro/Protobuf schemas via schema registry
attack_paths.impact: Downstream processing failures, data corruption, denial of service
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Schema registry accepts producer registrations; validation logic not shown

attack_paths.entry_point: Session token theft or MFA fatigue attack on platform engineers
attack_paths.impact: Full control over IAM policies, privilege escalation across all tiers
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: IAM service is central control plane; MFA bypass requires targeted social engineering

mitigations.control_name: Authentication and Authorization for Public-Facing Endpoints
Identity and Access Management with Least Privilege
File Integrity Monitoring on Ingestion Gateways
Code Signing and Verification for Flink/Spark Jobs
Data Loss Prevention for Cloud Storage
Anomaly Detection on Data Access Patterns
ML Data Validation and Drift Detection

findings.severity_rationale: Internet-facing webhook with no depicted WAF or auth allows unauthenticated RCE leading to Kafka cluster compromise
External producer credentials lack rotation enforcement; compromise enables data injection across pipeline
SFTP gateway lacks file integrity monitoring; web shell persistence enables ongoing ingestion manipulation
Airflow-to-Flink job submission path lacks code signing; insider or compromised Airflow achieves arbitrary code execution in processing tier
Raw data lake contains unencrypted PII/financial data with broad read access; compromised processing job enables mass exfiltration
BI dashboard service account has excessive warehouse read privileges; SQL injection or token theft exposes curated business data
Feature store lacks adversarial data detection; targeted poisoning via streaming pipeline degrades all downstream models
Model registry has signature verification but CI/CD pipeline not shown; supply chain compromise could deploy backdoored models
Schema registry accepts producer registrations without compatibility enforcement; malicious schemas cause downstream DoS
IAM service is single control plane; MFA bypass grants full policy control across all trust zones

agentic.blast_radius: ML serving endpoint can return predictions affecting downstream business decisions; feature store read access enables reconnaissance; warehouse query access enables data exfiltration
human_oversight_points: Model deployment approval gate in ML model registry
Automated drift detection alerts to ML ops team
